source: Publisher documentation saved under e3/truth/docs/fresh/ (sha256 in SHA256SUMS): TPC-DS v3.2.0; LDBC SNB specification (v2.2.5-SNAPSHOT, Appendix D for the Interactive v1 legacy data sets); GTFS Schedule Reference; FAA ardata.pdf (5/8/2025); ABS ASGS Edition 3 web pages; SEC Financial Statement Data Sets; College Scorecard Field of Study documentation (October 2026) and data dictionary; EPA AirData FileFormats (v3.0.0); 2024 ACS PUMS data dictionary and Census regions and divisions; City of Chicago portal metadata (ijzp-q8t2, c7ck-438e); USDA FoodData Central download field descriptions (October 2020)
rule: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the confirmatory evaluation, joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: EPA AirData daily summary file daily_44201_2025 (ozone, 2025; the file as downloaded for the confirmatory evaluation, 'As of' date in the README); single table filtered to Parameter Code 44201; dropped Parameter Code, Parameter Name and Units of Measure (constant: one parameter, reported in its standard unit) and Date of Last Change (record maintenance date).

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (Version 3.0.0), 2.1 Site Description File, Content: "A unique site is identified by the combination of state code, county code, and site number (within county). It can also be identified by the latitude and longitude."; 5.2 Daily Summary Format: "The monitoring site’s angular distance north of the equator measured in decimal degrees.", "The name of the site (if any) given by the State, local, or tribal air pollution control agency that operates it.", "The name of the core bases statistical area (metropolitan area) where the monitoring site is located."
truth.justification: The three codes identify the site, and these columns describe the site (its position, datum, name, address and the state, county, city and CBSA it lies in).

audit.quote: 2.1 Content: "Each unique geographic location that contains monitors is called a \"site\" in AQS. Information about the geographic setting is store in the site record, which are presented here. A unique site is identified by the combination of state code, county code, and site number (within county)."; 5.2: each right-hand side is defined as a property of the monitoring site, e.g. Latitude "The monitoring site’s angular distance north of the equator measured in decimal degrees.", Datum "The Datum associated with the Latitude and Longitude measures.", Local Site Name "The name of the site (if any) given by the State, local, or tribal air pollution control agency that operates it.", Address "The approximate street address of the monitoring site.", County Name "The name of the county where the monitoring site is located.", CBSA Name "The name of the core bases statistical area (metropolitan area) where the monitoring site is located."
audit.source: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (AirData Download Files Documentation, Version 3.0.0, December 01, 2015), 2.1 Site Description File - Content; 5.2 Daily Summary Files - Format

truth.clause: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (Version 3.0.0), 5.2: "An internal system code indicating the method (processes, equipment, and protocols) used in gathering and measuring the sample. The method name is in the next column."; 3.2 Monitor Description File: "A method code is only unique within a parameter (that is, method 111 for ozone is not the same as method 111 for benzene)."
truth.justification: (Parameter Code, Method Code) identifies a method and so its name; the relation is filtered to the single parameter 44201, so the dropped Parameter Code is constant and Method Code alone determines Method Name here (it does not across parameters).

audit.quote: 5.2 Method Code: "An internal system code indicating the method (processes, equipment, and protocols) used in gathering and measuring the sample. The method name is in the next column."; 3.2 Last Method Code: "A method code is only unique within a parameter (that is, method 111 for ozone is not the same as method 111 for benzene)."; construction: "filtered to Parameter Code 44201"
audit.source: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (AirData Download Files Documentation, Version 3.0.0, December 01, 2015), 5.2 Daily Summary Files - Format; 3.2 Monitor Description File - Format; construction of the relation

truth.clause: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (Version 3.0.0), 1.1 Monitors: "POC – Parameter Occurrence Code. Used to uniquely identify a monitor if there is more than one device measuring the same pollutant at the same site."; 5.1 Daily Summary Files, Content: "The daily summary files contain (at least) one record for each monitor that reported data for the given day. There may be multiple records for the monitor if:" (calculated sample durations, multiple standards, exceptional events)
truth.justification: A monitor (site, parameter, POC) has one record per day except for the three listed reasons, which Sample Duration, Pollutant Standard and Event Type distinguish; the documentation never declares this combination a key, so the record key is inferred and unsure.

audit.quote: 5.1 Content: "This file will contain a daily summary record that is: 1) The aggregate of all sub-daily measurements taken at the monitor." and "The daily summary files contain (at least) one record for each monitor that reported data for the given day. There may be multiple records for the monitor if: There are calculated sample durations for the pollutant. [...] There are multiple standards for the pollutant (q.v. pollutant standards). There were exceptional events associated with some measurements [...]"; 1.2: "So the annual and daily summary files will (possibly) contain multiple records that have been calculated using different rules and starting metrics. These are differentiated by the Pollutant Standard."; 5.2 Event Type: "If an event occurred for the parameter in question, the data will have multiple records for each monitor."; 1.1: "Identified by: The site (state + county + site number) where the monitor is located AND The pollutant code AND POC"
audit.source: epa_aqs_FileFormats.html (AirData Download Files Documentation, Version 3.0.0, December 01, 2015), 1.1 Monitors; 1.2 Pollutant Standards; 5.1 Daily Summary Files - Content; 5.2 Event Type
